name: hubspot
label: HubSpot
note: HubSpot's APIs with a private app access token. OAuth apps mint tokens that expire and are refreshed by the app itself; those are not what this stores.

name: close
label: Close
note: The Close REST API with an API key from Settings, sent as the basic-auth username with no password. Close does not scope its keys, so the key carries everything the user who made it can reach.

name: attio
label: Attio
note: Attio's REST API with a single-workspace access token from Workspace settings. The token carries the scopes chosen when it was made, so a call outside those scopes fails even though the key is good.

name: keap
label: Keap
note: Keap's REST API with a personal access token or a service account key. A service account key is account-wide admin access and only an admin can mint one; a personal access token acts as one user and is the safer paste.

name: insightly
template_hint: the region in your Insightly API URL under User Settings, such as na1 or eu1
label: Insightly
note: Insightly's v3.1 API with the key sent as the basic-auth username and no password. The pod is Insightly's own region rather than your subdomain, so it is shared with other tenants and the key alone identifies the account.

name: apollo
label: Apollo.io
note: Apollo's API with a workspace API key. One key reads and writes the whole workspace — contacts, accounts, sequences and email activity — and cannot be narrowed to read-only from here.

name: streak
label: Streak
note: Streak's API with the key as the basic-auth username and no password. The key belongs to a person's Gmail account rather than a service account, so it reaches whatever that mailbox can see.

name: hunter
label: Hunter
note: Hunter's email finder and verifier with an account API key as a bearer token. Hunter also accepts the same key as an api_key query parameter, which puts a live credential in URLs and logs; this route never does that.

name: salesloft
label: Salesloft
note: Salesloft's API with a long-lived API key carrying the scopes granted at creation. Salesloft will not approve a partner application authenticated this way, so it is for your own account only.

name: chili-piper
label: Chili Piper
note: Chili Piper's Edge API with a token from Command Center, shown once and scoped to the permission set it was issued against. Their spec also allows the key as an apiKey query parameter; this route sends it as a header instead.

name: dealfront
label: Dealfront
note: Dealfront's current Leadfeeder API with a personal API key. The key is not subject to OAuth scope checks, so it sees every account its owner sees; the older API at docs.leadfeeder.com uses a different header and is not what this reaches.

name: reply-io
label: Reply.io
note: Reply.io's v3 API with the account key from Settings. It is one account-wide credential with no per-scope restriction, and the v1 x-api-key header it replaced is no longer accepted.

name: instantly
label: Instantly
note: Instantly's v2 API with a key carrying the scopes chosen when it was created. A v1 key will not work here.

name: capsule-crm
label: Capsule CRM
note: Capsule's v2 API with a personal access token from My Preferences. The token carries the full access of the person who made it; Capsule offers no read-only personal token.

name: affinity
label: Affinity
note: Affinity's v2 API, which takes the key as a bearer token. v2 is not yet at parity with v1, and v1 authenticates a different way, so anything v1-only is out of reach through this route.

name: folk
label: folk
note: folk's API with a workspace API key. The key reaches the whole workspace — people, companies, deals, notes and tasks — with no narrower scope offered at creation.

name: twenty
label: Twenty
note: Twenty's hosted cloud API with a key from Settings. A self-hosted Twenty lives on your own domain and is not reachable through this entry; give us that address instead.

name: follow-up-boss
label: Follow Up Boss
note: Follow Up Boss's API with the key as the basic-auth username and a blank password. The key inherits the access of the user who created it, so an admin's key reaches every contact in the account.

name: salesflare
label: Salesflare
note: Salesflare's API with a key from Settings. The key acts as the user who made it across accounts, contacts, opportunities and pipelines; Salesflare offers no per-key scoping.

name: people-data-labs
label: People Data Labs
note: People Data Labs enrichment and search with the key in a header. PDL also accepts it as an api_key query parameter, which would put a live credential in URL logs; this route never does.

name: rocketreach
label: RocketReach
note: RocketReach lookups with the key in the Api-Key header — not the more usual X-Api-Key, and the wrong one fails as a plain 401 with nothing to say why. Lookups spend credits; the account path used to check this route does not.

name: findymail
label: Findymail
note: Findymail email finding and verification, served from the app host rather than an api. subdomain. Each found email spends a credit; reading the balance does not.

name: anymailfinder
label: Anymail Finder
note: Anymail Finder with the key sent bare in the Authorization header, with no Bearer word in front of it. Their error for a bad key cannot tell a wrong key from a client that added the word back.

name: leadmagic
label: LeadMagic
note: LeadMagic's REST API for email, mobile and B2B enrichment against one credit balance. Only the REST surface takes a static key: their CLI signs in through a browser and their hosted MCP server uses OAuth, and neither will accept a key stored here.

name: wiza
label: Wiza
note: Wiza contact reveal and list export, served from the main site host rather than an api. subdomain. Reveals are asynchronous — you start a job and poll it — so this is not a single-call enrichment API.

name: surfe
label: Surfe
note: Surfe people and company search and enrichment, with separate email, mobile and search credit pools. Bulk enrichment is start-a-job-then-poll rather than a single call.

name: calendly
label: Calendly
note: Calendly's REST API with a personal access token from the API and webhooks page. Calendly does not store or redisplay the token after it is generated, so a lost one has to be replaced rather than recovered.

name: cal-com
label: Cal.com
note: Cal.com's v2 API with a cal_live_ key as a bearer token. The v1 API took its key as a query parameter instead and is not what this reaches.

name: savvycal
label: SavvyCal
note: SavvyCal's API with a private key created in developer settings. It reads and writes your own account only; SavvyCal's OAuth flow is what covers other people's accounts, and this does not perform it.

name: common-room
label: Common Room
note: Common Room's Core API with a token created by a room admin. The token is community-wide; there is no narrower scope to issue.

name: coresignal
label: Coresignal
note: Coresignal's company and employee data API with the key in an apikey header. There is no free account endpoint — the balance is returned as a header on ordinary calls — so every read here spends a credit.

name: woodpecker
label: Woodpecker
note: Woodpecker's REST API. Keys are per-user rather than per-workspace, so a key reaches only the campaigns and prospects of the person who made it and a colleague's sequences stay invisible.

name: mailshake
label: Mailshake
note: Mailshake's API with the key as the basic-auth username. The key never expires and cannot be scoped, and Mailshake echoes it back inside its own error bodies, so those responses are not safe to log.

name: overloop
label: Overloop
note: Overloop's public API with the key sent bare in the Authorization header, no scheme word in front. One account-wide credential covering prospects, organisations, deals and automations; there is no read-only variant.

name: amplemarket
label: Amplemarket
note: Amplemarket's API with an account-wide key. The people-search and enrichment endpoints it reaches are metered, so this key spends credits, and its rate limit is shared by everything using it.

name: heyreach
label: HeyReach
note: HeyReach's public API for LinkedIn campaigns and inboxes. The key is account-wide; their separate hosted MCP server is a different surface and will not read a key stored here.

name: avoma
label: Avoma
note: Avoma's meeting, transcript and scorecard API. The token is not self-service — Avoma support issues it — and every path ends in a slash, so a request without one is redirected rather than answered.

name: uplead
label: UpLead
note: UpLead contact and company search with the key sent bare in the Authorization header, no scheme word. Lookups spend credits; reading the balance does not.

name: breakcold
label: Breakcold
note: Breakcold's public REST API with a scoped key from Settings, shown once at creation. The key carries the scopes chosen then, so a call outside them returns 403 even though the key is good.
